results.title: GACL’s GH¢30m dividend Is manufactured and misleading – Africa Policy Lens
results.content: The Africa Policy Lens (APL) says the much-publicised GH¢30 million dividend by the Ghana Airports Company Limited (GACL) to Government is manufactured and does not reflect operational performance. In a statement issued by its Research Directorate, APL said it had examined GACL's 2025 Audited Accounts as presented at its 11th Annual General Meeting and concluded that the dividend is being misrepresented as evidence of a turnaround.

results.title: KNUST, Lands Ministry explore plans for satellite campus in Ellembelle to honour Nkrumah
results.content: The Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) is exploring plans to establish a satellite campus in Ellembelle in the Western Region in honour of Ghana's first President, Dr Kwame Nkrumah. The proposal emerged from discussions between the university's Vice-Chancellor, Professor Christian Agyare, and the Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, during a visit to the university on Tuesday, November 3, 2026. The proposed campus is expected to expand access to higher education in the Nzema area and strengthen KNUST's presence in the Western Region, particularly within the country's oil and gas enclave. The initiative is also intended to recognise Dr Nkrumah's contribution to Ghana's independence, industrialisation and educational development.

results.title: Fifi Kwetey explains why he is comfortable without a government board role
results.content: The General Secretary of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Fifi Kwetey, says he has not been offered a government board appointment, describing the situation as one that gives him greater freedom to speak independently on issues affecting the party and government. Speaking on JoyNews' PM Express, Mr Kwetey said he had neither sought nor asked for a board position, although he would have considered an offer if the role was not full-time. "I've not gone looking for it. I've not gone asking for it and stuff like that. If they had offered, would you have accepted? Why not? I wouldn't have minded. Because as long as it's not a full-time position, if it's not a full-time position that will hold me, I mean, it's not a problem," he said.

results.title: NDC will not shield officials involved in wrongdoing – Fifi Kwetey
results.content: The General Secretary of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Fifi Kwetey, says the party will not shield any of its members or government appointees found culpable of wrongdoing, insisting that President John Dramani Mahama shares its commitment to accountability. Speaking on JoyNews' PM Express, Mr Kwetey said the party was determined to seek answers whenever concerns about possible wrongdoing emerged, rather than rush to defend those involved. He said the approach represented a departure from what he described as a previous tendency among political organisations to protect their members when allegations arose.

results.title: When applause replaces discernment
results.content: There is something about the recent exchanges among some prominent Ghanaian religious leaders that deserves more attention than it is receiving. The focus has largely been on what one pastor said about other prophets, who has responded, who has taken offence and who has insulted whom. But I believe we are overlooking an equally important part of the story: the people sitting in the congregations, listening, clapping, cheering and sometimes appearing visibly delighted as their pastors attack fellow ministers from the pulpit.

results.title: Connecting Africa’s wallets, unlocking Africa’s trade, smartly
results.content: Yesterday, Monday, 2 November, I joined discussions at the 15th Africa Internet Governance Forum at the Labadi Beach Hotel in Accra, including a Smart Africa Steering Committee roundtable. My main message was that connecting Africa’s mobile money wallets across borders, alongside visa-free travel, could transform intra-African trade, significantly. At the Africa Prosperity Network (APN), we estimate that implementing both reforms could help raise intra-African trade from around 16% to more than 25% within five years. The opportunity is enormous. The figures I presented show that US$2.1 trillion flowed through mobile money wallets globally in 2025, with approximately US$1.4 trillion, two-thirds of the total, transacted in sub-Saharan Africa. results.title: GIS investigates explosion that killed officer during Hamile border patrol
results.content: The Ghana Immigration Service (GIS) is investigating an explosion during a border patrol operation in the Hamile Sector of the Upper West Region that killed one of its officers and a tricycle rider. The incident occurred in the early hours of Tuesday, November 3, 2026, along an unapproved route in the border area, according to a statement issued by the Service. The GIS said a team of four officers on patrol responded to an unusual sound and intercepted a man transporting a load on a tricycle. The rider reportedly attempted to flee as the officers approached to inspect the contents of the load. “In the process of trying to stop him, the load exploded, resulting in the death of the tricycle rider and injuries to two officers,” the statement said.
